description: An animated, tileable ocean patch for a water plane. A detail wrangle picks the waves once: a main swell of wave_length running with the wind, three more swells around it and sixteen small waves on top, each a whole number of waves across the patch (the way an FFT ocean tile is built, so copies of the patch join without a seam), their heights adding up to wave_height. A point wrangle moves them with time (deep-water speeds) as Gerstner waves whose crests choppiness pulls together, while every vertex stays on the regular grid (it solves for the wave that lands on it), so the patch stays exactly size by size; it writes exact normals, a foam value where the crests are squeezed together, and Cd from deep water to pale foam (the water material is white, so Cd is the colour: export with vertex colours). The render shows nine copies of the patch side by side.

wave_height.desc: height of the largest swells above sea level (m); no point rises or sinks further

wave_length.desc: distance between the largest swells (m), rounded so whole swells fit across the patch (at most size)

choppiness.desc: how sharp the crests are: 0 round swells, 1 peaked crests with plenty of foam

wind_direction.desc: where the waves run to (degrees counter-clockwise from +X, seen from above)

vertex_spacing.desc: distance between the surface's vertices (m); a patch has at most 400 x 400 quads, so a large patch with a fine spacing gets coarser

seed.desc: random seed of the waves' directions, lengths and phases (the sea state stays)

params.names: kx kz amp omega phase hx hz

params.label: size
params.expr: abs(bbox.min.x + size / 2) < 0.001 && abs(bbox.max.x - size / 2) < 0.001 && abs(bbox.min.z + size / 2) < 0.001 && abs(bbox.max.z - size / 2) < 0.001

surface.label: Ocean surface
surface.description: The water surface at the current frame: a size x size grid centred on the origin at sea level (y = 0), tileable, with uv, normals, a point foam value 0..1 and Cd, in the water material.
